scope: Theorem 4.11 (Amalgamation at closed levels) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an unbounded class of strong-limit cardinals µ of countable cofinality with the following properties. 1. K is categorical in µ, and any two µ-sized strong extensions of a µ-model have a strong amalgam of size µ. 2. If A ≤K B0, B1 all have size µ, and di ∈ Bi are tuples of the same length at most σ < µ, there is such an amalgam identifying d0 with d1 if and only if D(d0, X; B0) = D(d1, X; B1) for every X ⊆ A, |X| ≤ g(σ). 3. There are at most µ singleton types over each µ-model, where type means identification in an amalgam over that model. One may take every sufficiently large strong-limit cardinal of countable cofinality strictly closed under t and g.
